ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: High-contrast distribution with approximately 65% high-intensity white pixels concentrated in the central lobe regions and 35% low-intensity black pixels located primarily along the trailing edges and in linear streaks.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Contiguous high-intensity white regions occupy the central 70% of both lobes. These are bordered by a continuous black perimeter on the trailing edge. Vertical black streaks and circular focal spots (approximately 10-15 distinct marks) are distributed across the white spatial area.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep V-shaped depression with a calculated internal pixel angle of approximately 55 degrees and a vertical depth occupying roughly 15% of the total fluke height.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: Highly irregular, high-amplitude serrations along the entire boundary. Extraction shows frequent peaks and valleys with a pixel depth variation of up to 20 pixels from the mean edge trajectory, creating a jagged silhouette.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: The trailing edge follows a wide convex curve from the median notch toward the distal tips, heavily modified by localized geometric irregularities.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: High-contrast yellowish-white pixel clusters (barnacle colonies) are densely concentrated on the distal tips and at irregular intervals along the trailing edge peaks.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Significant detection of parallel and unaligned vertical black linear disruptions (rake marks) that intersect the white pigmentation, particularly dense on the medial section of the right lobe.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Extensive barnacle colonization on the fluke tips and trailing edge; multiple vertical linear scars (rake marks) across the ventral surface.
other_distinctive_markers: Extreme degree of trailing edge serration and fragmentation relative to typical smooth-edge variations.
